page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 vCPUs running on a single dedicated physical AMD EPYC 9B45 processor core with 2 threads per core. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is allocated at 7.0 GB of RAM, or 3.5 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector instruction sets including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16) and cryptographic accelerators (AES, VAES, SHA-NI) are fully enabled. The instance includes no local storage or GPUs, relying on external network-attached volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark results highlight an asymmetry between single-threaded and multi-threaded throughput due to the single-core configuration. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-threaded tasks, such as stress-ng single-core compute (3471.18), single-threaded gzip compression (37.77 GB/sec), bzip3 decompression (16.86 GB/sec), and Geekbench text processing (2873.0). Conversely, aggregate multi-core tests—including multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core (3234.0), and PassMark CPU score (4671.15)—fall into the bottom 25% of evaluated cloud servers. Memory throughput sits in the middle tier for large uncached transfers (45.8 GB/sec read, 30.63 GB/sec write), while cached small-block operations exhibit lower relative bandwidth.

The qualitative cost profile makes the c4d-standard-2 an efficient option for light execution paths demanding modern single-core execution speed without provisioning large core counts. Because it pairs modern AMD EPYC silicon with a modest 7.0 GB memory footprint and no bundled NVMe storage, resource waste is minimized for entry-level services. It is appropriate for lightweight web serving, single-threaded batch compression, basic CI/CD utility tasks, and auxiliary microservices, but it represents a poor fit for parallelized computing, heavy compilation, or dense in-memory databases.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-2 is an entry-tier general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 2 vCPUs from a single dedicated physical AMD EPYC 9B45 core and 7.0 GB of memory (3.5 GB per vCPU). Utilizing x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 and hardware cryptographic instructions, the instance delivers top-tier single-core performance, demonstrated by high scores in single-threaded stress-ng, gzip compression, and text processing. However, due to its single physical core constraint, multi-core metrics, PassMark scores, and database operation benchmarks rank in the lower quartile. The instance features no local storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external block storage for operation. With a moderate memory allocation and strong per-core instruction efficiency, the c4d-standard-2 provides a balanced, cost-conscious environment for lightweight web servers, microservices, small CI/CD tasks, and low-concurrency single-threaded utilities.

bullet_points: Powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9B45 physical core (2 vCPUs) with 32 MB L3 cache
7.0 GB system memory (3.5 GB per vCPU) with middle-tier uncached bandwidth
Features advanced vector extensions including AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators
Zero bundled local NVMe storage and no integrated GPU accelerators
Top-tier single-core and compression performance with limited multi-core scaling
Suited for light web hosting, microservices, small utilities, and single-threaded batch scripts
